_readme: Local record of policy and macro events that shape the Uzbek housing market.
The agent merges these with live web research. Entries here are treated as
prior knowledge and are labelled in the report by their `confidence` value.
Add your own entries freely - this file is meant to be edited. Fields:
date            ISO date the measure took effect or was announced (required)
title           short name of the measure
category        policy | monetary | fiscal | macro | regulatory | demographic
summary         one or two sentences on what it did
expected_impact how it should move housing demand, supply, prices or credit
direction       positive | negative | mixed | neutral  (effect on housing prices)
confidence      high | medium | low - how sure you are of the details
still_in_force  true if it still shapes the market outside the data window
source          URL backing the entry (strongly recommended)
Set "example": true on any entry you want the agent to ignore.

events.title: Foreign exchange liberalisation
events.summary: Uzbekistan abolished the multiple exchange rate system and let the som float, unifying the official and parallel market rates.
events.expected_impact: Repriced imported construction materials and dollar-denominated savings, and reset the som value of housing. Marks the start of the modern, market-priced housing cycle.

events.title: Transition of the Central Bank to inflation targeting
events.summary: A presidential decree set out the Central Bank's move to an inflation-targeting regime, making the policy rate the main instrument of monetary policy.
events.expected_impact: Made mortgage rates responsive to the policy rate, so housing demand became sensitive to monetary policy decisions.

events.title: Uzbekistan Mortgage Refinancing Company (UzMRC)
events.summary: A state-backed mortgage refinancing institution was set up with international financial institution support to give banks long-term funding for housing loans.
events.expected_impact: Lengthens mortgage tenors and expands lending capacity, supporting demand for primary-market housing.

events.title: Energy tariff liberalisation
events.summary: Regulated electricity and gas tariffs were raised substantially as part of the phased withdrawal of energy subsidies.
events.expected_impact: Raises construction and building-material costs and squeezes household budgets, pushing new-build costs up while weakening affordability.
